meta.title_he: קומת משרדי איירונסורס, מגדל שרונה, תל אביב (2017)
meta.era: 2017 high-tech fit-out (RUST architects) in the 2017 Azrieli Sarona Tower

source.title: ArchDaily: IronSource / RUST architects, floor plan (image 48 of 50, floor_Plan_15), with scale bar
source.license: Published plan, used only as a reference for dimensions

assumptions: Scale 28.4 px/m from the drawn bar (2.5 m = 71 px); the box comes to 44.3 x 60.6 m with about 2,387 m2 indoors; ArchDaily gives 10,000 m2 for the whole fit-out, i.e. about four floors of this size
The ArchDaily page names neither the building nor the floor; officesnapshots places ironSource in Azrieli Sarona Tower, and the plan is taken as one typical office floor
Clear ceiling height 3.0 m: not on the plan; the tower is 238.5 m over 61 floors (about 3.9 m floor to floor), minus slab and services

Both cores are drawn rotated about 10 degrees and are squared on their centre lines: core faces are up to about 1.5 m off at the core ends; the slanted NW and SE wing facades and the SE room fronts are squared too
Outdoor notches (north between the wings, south between the SW and SE wings) are labelled outside and fenced with the curtain wall, so they leave the coverage shares
Facade: coated curtain wall all round (Sarona Tower is fully glazed); no openable windows or shutters
Core walls drawn about 0.40 m thick: modelled with the 40 cm RC row (shelter_40; it is not a shelter)
Lift shafts: 20 cm RC walls with closed steel landing doors (door_steel); lift cars as solid metal
Shafts, toilets and plant rooms inside the service core simplified to six rooms (risers drawn as metal ducts in the toilet blocks); toilet walls block 10
Room-divider walls double gypsum, room fronts single-pane glass; walls read to about +-0.3 m
Team-room doors open, meeting-room, office and service doors closed; fire-stair door closed (code)

The 'comm box' is the floor communications room drawn at the service core's east face; AP1 goes on the ceiling in the east corridor right outside it (clear of the fire stair that juts into the corridor)
One AP only (the library rule: the first one an installer hangs), so most of the floor shows no service; the council's grid check needed about 24 APs at 11 m to bring no service down to about 8 %
Meeting rooms north of the core take their only doors in their glass north fronts (the core face has none)
Desks, sofas and tables drawn where the plan shows them; they carry no radio loss
No mamak is marked on this plan; it is not modelled
No wall uses its own loss_db: every value is the materials table's
israeli_features: Twin reinforced-concrete core of a Tel Aviv supertall: six lift banks, three lift lobbies, fire stair
Floor comm box ('comm box' on the plan, the floor wiring closet) beside the core, where the ISP fibre and the AP cabling start
Glass-fronted team rooms round the facade, double-gypsum dividers, coffee bar with island (pinat kafe)
Bike room in the core for Tel Aviv cycling commuters
Fully glazed coated curtain wall (Sarona Tower)
meta.notes: One floor of ironSource's four-floor HQ in Azrieli Sarona Tower: team rooms ring the glass facade and two thick concrete cores (lifts, and toilets / shafts / stair) fill the middle. A single ceiling AP by the comm box covers the east side only; the cores block almost everything behind them, so the west wing, the lift lobbies and the far south and north rooms get no service. A real install needs an AP grid on the corridor ring round the cores (the council's check used about 24 APs on an 11 m grid). The coated curtain wall (about 32 dB at 5 GHz in the table) also keeps Wi-Fi from neighbouring towers out.
